  - heading "How do I help my child become a fluent reader at home?" [level=2]
  - text: To help your child become a fluent reader at home,
  - mark:
    - text: focus on activities that balance
    - strong: accuracy, speed, and expression (prosody)
  - text: . Fluency is the vital bridge to reading comprehension because it frees up brain power from sounding out words to actually understanding the story.
  - link "YouTube · Learning At The Primary Pond":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESaQHrOzAVWneFiWUMQcnwdPzRYWqQEu1RyHah2zxnrjlnv4CNX8berWoFTlt3nn9hzI4fWdqOJ9wOtXA7A0sqQzI91k7YRYmrdOf27JPoFolXqCRmo3Zz1luZecRzZSQ2k8PeMDpGs3dKBg

    - generic: "+1"
  - generic: "Here are the most effective, research-backed strategies you can use at home:"
  - heading "1. Model Fluent Reading (You Read First)" [level=3]
  - text: Children need to hear what fluent reading sounds like.
  - link "Reading Rockets":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESmAEB6zswFQ5QGFFY-DBCKQ4ybbHJMncBjEuDLgyqNSzkBmVCSY2V527cWBsZ7iVOJzRXWpR0lMGN1u7iZjOn8LEBC1D0loPCKwi5JraWNOH_bJvgtff_qpqrDasAlxNTA03gSR0nwi58IesGHy0d1gJQAINveyYS3gBopQjNIWVqtqFHzVNiajLSKqzgQEn6qCabjBJgFh47EA
  - button "Reading Rockets - Related results":
    - generic: Reading Rockets
  - list:
    - strong: "Read aloud daily:"
    - text: Read with a steady pace, pause at punctuation, and use exaggerated expression for different characters.
    - strong: "Use Audiobooks:"
    - text: Have your child follow along in a printed book while listening to an expert narrator. Free platforms like
    - link "Storyline Online":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVt9PecRGKIGvXBbO-IPTyH3yUxvDzA0wt22G-xVujYPrAHYiDFSFsIPSXDL_aPXtXTjXi4OZFQn2FPHCpT8inuBPLTg5xVb-CQ0rGJg0FPg
    - text: or PBS Kids offer excellent celebrity-read books.

  - heading "2. Practice Shared Reading Techniques" [level=3]
  - text: Instead of making your child read an entire book alone, share the load to reduce frustration.
  - link "Think Academy US":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESkQEB6zswFVQ70xVh8iRT1ETJxw9-MoSPHKA-Mo2863QEeWiElgVzCDpz3R-4fneqe2OycmkR8tyscLwj7FAjUwHsGaVCGaQT2Ez-CmUjXK7819cKK2vA73xw0zJagVH6GboQD92jOhhKkwjxY5rON5HEIhhMRXXaf6EAylWdEIwLODaQy0-xgRFO7dKqcd_zLwz9
  - button "Think Academy US (+1) - Related results":
    - generic: Think Academy US
    - generic: "+1"
  - list:
    - strong: "Echo Reading:"
    - text: Read one sentence aloud using great expression, then have your child immediately "echo" it back to you, mimicking your tone and pace.
    - link "Understood":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESngEB6zswFVGfvHRR5xR2apWhwwaU_LT7bdqBRTjCOZOgkrBzmtjgeLmXQ59BOZAhyj5tvuajhkkCrT9E-gYatxbIplAG2vnOvKt9km1CYNvHZk5sq_YXFxq8N3AGfxOnxg3lENohHoOYmYxh8J-Zs2dQInYf4Yl7KuPWsxFQlRczD4VFUY1iVZ-E4IC7mmLiJUtlRIjFCYP0CF3SRYV2Bw
    - button "Understood (+1) - Related results":
      - generic: Understood
      - generic: "+1"
    - strong: "Choral / Buddy Reading:"
    - text: Sit together and read the exact same passage out loud at the exact same time so they can match your voice. You can also take turns page-by-page.
    - link "Start with a Book":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVVIsf7XBj7qa6qguBUIevpDJxy7ikbsfzkpIrou64PoE7GyIeiMa7mULchqCzLzpK_A-ShSXtjRxreRvWHM6KB9e0Y5h-89oFSKfpX6UVWLLcIQal_03KIH32W0twb04jUA

  - heading "3. Emphasize \"Repeated Readings\"" [level=3]
  - text: Reading the same text multiple times is one of the fastest ways to build confidence and speed.
  - link "YouTube · Reading SOS with Alison":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAV-lACdyd3UWobDdMt-ToN8StPlJK-2fCzXfEdU6u-VEq9P89LpmbdguYF-FKjYVR0oWBLr8nyK9T-RVwMEj8d95Yv7_1id7xyac0ILnDJVeq92QwXGpcPN7VuX5lWFw
  - button "YouTube · Reading SOS with Alison (+1) - Related results":
    - generic: YouTube
    - generic: ·Reading SOS with Alison
    - generic: "+1"
  - list:
    - strong: "Reread Favorites:"
    - text: Don't worry if your child wants to read the same book over and over. Each pass builds faster word recognition.
    - strong: "Use Shorter Passages:"
    - text: Pick a short 100-word excerpt or poem. Have them practice reading it 3 to 5 times until it flows smoothly before moving on.
    - link "Reading Eggs":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAEShAEB6zswFVyukWOZPW1NPe_w71tGmbV0718MxN6DNPbFjUelOyWv0sKBWupgjIJuc7owLYeOHynxnYdzrtsXqlsCMAsw4F14Zyfj25WU3AZKG26qJVsNEATsaVk6W6kUKYc8Ek4TAhzYJV_dD4blQM2gebEuEQ6aD1DaXIXRVvSfXi8kHTs
    - button "Reading Eggs (+3) - Related results":
      - generic: Reading Eggs
      - generic: "+3"
  - heading "4. Try Text Chunking and Tracking" [level=3]
  - list:
    - strong: "Scoop the Words:"
    - text: Help your child group words into meaningful phrases rather than reading word-by-word. You can physically draw pencil "scoops" or forward slashes (
    - code: //
    - text: ) under phrases in a sentence to show them where to pause.
    - link "Understood":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESngEB6zswFVGfvHRR5xR2apWhwwaU_LT7bdqBRTjCOZOgkrBzmtjgeLmXQ59BOZAhyj5tvuajhkkCrT9E-gYatxbIplAG2vnOvKt9km1CYNvHZk5sq_YXFxq8N3AGfxOnxg3lENohHoOYmYxh8J-Zs2dQInYf4Yl7KuPWsxFQlRczD4VFUY1iVZ-E4IC7mmLiJUtlRIjFCYP0CF3SRYV2Bw
    - button "Understood (+1) - Related results":
      - generic: Understood
      - generic: "+1"
    - strong: "Finger Tracking:"
    - text: Encourage them to run their finger or a fun pointer (like a small paintbrush) smoothly under the words as they read to keep their place and maintain momentum.
    - link "NWEA":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESjgEB6zswFXZOiZ7sKINSvsecHqSCQeTLGYhiMJ0f3m72SC7JrmZB7DLlUhs47jNYvEYYuPynnN2sL2DuZ8E4baT7CS3okTgDuzVyG0TZSkmuFPNGvu_D92xapEObvnpxPPwqS4oOrHE0JB8JRbLzB5M7uEzWctzwnRUgzUrCAOMI8NUyw-7mpZiavYYeBNuS
    - button "NWEA - Related results":

  - heading "5. Use the \"Pause, Prompt, Praise\" Rule" [level=3]
  - text: When your child gets stuck on a word, resist the urge to jump in immediately.
  - link "NWEA":
    - /url: /goto?url=CAESjgEB6zswFXZOiZ7sKINSvsecHqSCQeTLGYhiMJ0f3m72SC7JrmZB7DLlUhs47jNYvEYYuPynnN2sL2DuZ8E4baT7CS3okTgDuzVyG0TZSkmuFPNGvu_D92xapEObvnpxPPwqS4oOrHE0JB8JRbLzB5M7uEzWctzwnRUgzUrCAOMI8NUyw-7mpZiavYYeBNuS
  - button "NWEA - Related results":
    - generic: NWEA
  - list:
    - strong: "Pause:"
    - text: Give them 4 to 5 seconds to try sounding it out or self-correcting.
    - strong: "Prompt:"
    - text: If they are completely stuck, offer a small phonetic clue (e.g., "Look at the vowel team") or ask a question to get them back on track.
    - strong: "Praise:"
    - text: Focus your praise on their
    - emphasis: effort
    - text: and specific successes rather than just getting through the book.
    - link "95 Percent Group":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESqQEB6zswFVBQaFBN_IkPBEQIo5_oUGc5_90oKfNCXS_BfLjHBpuXsJro0F9Rgfvi53R4UNUouYzyq_3M78VatwIJrN02x8FSrAeuRRTNI7Xeo65AU4kMTpHlzP6mkbvcNn7Q0CHb3x3Ygd67peO28b7mCLTaSdQMLqaz5TSB6PMJZm6VsYQELv9CXWzOnzUC2e6HRAQZWRgCphm6d0mYaiTBqNE-BL9kitFg
    - button "95 Percent Group (+1) - Related results":
      - generic: 95 Percent Group
      - generic: "+1"
  - heading "6. Make It Playful" [level=3]
  - list:
    - strong: "Reader’s Theater:"
    - text: Print out simple, short scripts. Assign roles, ham it up with silly voices, and rehearse it multiple times. No costumes or memorization needed—just fun expression.
